newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela approves oil company restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela approves oil company restructuring.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) has a major restructuring of its business units to cut costs and improve efficiency, PDVSA sources said on Monday.

Directors of the holding company PDVSA and its three affiliates, Maraven, Lagoven and Corpoven, agreed the changes with Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta at a closed-door meeting between Thursday and Saturday last week, they said.

They are due to be introduced from August until early next year and involve dissolving the three main subsidiaries to create more focused business units. Each of the three affiliates currently duplicate functions as three vertically integrated companies.

"Corpoven, Lagoven and Maraven are going to disappear and there will be new subsidiaries, one E+P, one supply, trading and manufacturing, and one for other services, but these will be new companies," the source said.
"Obviously what is driving this is cost reduction. The strategic change in direction was approved, but the details still have to be decided," he added.
Some jobs would be lost through natural wastage, but there would be no negative effect on international agreements, the source said.
